description: Add the customer review submission form to the product detail page, wire it to POST /api/v1/reviews, and display approved reviews fetched live from GET /api/v1/reviews. Also update the Rating component and product detail reviews section to show real DB review counts and approved reviews. Depends on FEAT-001 (api.ts hooks useReviews, api.submitReview must exist).
steps:
Step 1 — Add a `ReviewForm` component to src/components/veloura/shopping-ui.tsx. The backend POST /api/v1/reviews expects: `{ product_id?: string; customer_name: string; rating: number; title?: string; body?: string }`. Reviews are created with `approved: false` — they go live after admin approval. Component signature: `export function ReviewForm({ productId }: { productId: string })` Implementation: - Import `useMutation`, `useQueryClient` from '@tanstack/react-query'. - Import `api`, `apiEnabled` from '@/lib/api'. - Import `Star` from 'lucide-react'. - State: name (string), rating (number, 0 = unset), title (string), body (string), submitted (bool). - useMutation calling `api.submitReview({ product_id: productId, customer_name: name, rating, title, body })`. - On success: show a thank-you message 'Your review has been submitted for approval.'. - Render: star selector (1–5 clickable stars), name input (required), title input (optional), textarea for body (optional), submit button. - If `!apiEnabled`: render `

Reviews require the backend to be running.

`. - Accessibility: fieldset+legend for star rating, proper labels for all inputs.

Step 2 — Add a `LiveReviews` component to src/components/veloura/shopping-ui.tsx that shows approved reviews from the DB.
  - Import `useReviews` from '@/lib/api'.
  - Signature: `export function LiveReviews({ productId, fallbackCount }: { productId: string; fallbackCount: number })`
  - Call `const { data } = useReviews(productId);`
  - Filter: `const productReviews = data?.reviews?.filter(r => r.product_id === productId) ?? [];`
  - If `productReviews.length`: render them as `<blockquote>` elements matching the existing static review blockquote style in ProductDetailPage (border-t border-border pt-5, text-sm body, footer with name and date).
  - If `!productReviews.length && !apiEnabled`: render the two existing static demo review blockquotes from ProductDetailPage (to preserve existing look).
  - If `!productReviews.length && apiEnabled`: render 'Be the first to leave a review.'.
  - Export the average rating too for the Rating component: `export function useProductRating(productId: string, fallback: number) { const { data } = useReviews(productId); const filtered = data?.reviews?.filter(r => r.product_id === productId) ?? []; return filtered.length ? filtered.reduce((s,r) => s + r.rating, 0) / filtered.length : fallback; }`

Step 3 — Update the reviews section in `ProductDetailPage` inside src/components/veloura/commerce.tsx. The current reviews section (near bottom of ProductDetailPage) is: ```tsx
{['Beautifully cut...', 'An easy addition...'].map((review, i) => ...)}
``` Replace with: ```tsx

Leave a Review

``` Add imports for `LiveReviews` and `ReviewForm` from '@/components/veloura/shopping-ui'.

Step 4 — Update the `Rating` component in src/components/veloura/shopping-ui.tsx to show live rating when available.
  - Import `useProductRating` from same file (defined in Step 2 above — it's in the same file so no import needed, just call it).
  - In the `Rating` component, call `const liveRating = useProductRating(product.id, product.rating);`.
  - Change the displayed rating from `{product.rating}` to `{liveRating > 0 ? liveRating.toFixed(1) : product.rating}`.
  - Change the review count label: if apiEnabled and live reviews exist, show `({liveCount} reviews)` instead of `({product.reviewCount} demo reviews)`. Build `liveCount` the same way `useProductRating` does (call `useReviews` in Rating too, or accept it as prop — simpler to call `useReviews` directly).
  - Keep the Star icon and layout unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build completes with zero TypeScript errors
The product detail page shows a 'Leave a Review' section with a star selector, name field, and submit button
Submitting the form calls POST /api/v1/reviews when VITE_API_URL is set; shows 'submitted for approval' confirmation
After approving a review in the admin panel, the product detail page shows it in the reviews section within 30 seconds (next refetch cycle)
When VITE_API_URL is not set, the static demo reviews render and the form shows the 'requires backend' message
verification: npm run build  (from project root — must succeed with zero errors)

With VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:8000: navigate to any product page, submit a review, see 'submitted for approval' message; approve it in admin at http://localhost:8000/admin, reload product page and see it appear
findings: All 4 steps implemented. shopping-ui.tsx: added useProductRating hook, updated Rating component to call useReviews(product.id) and show live average+count (falls back to static when apiEnabled=false), added ReviewForm (useMutation calling api.submitReview, star selector, name/title/body fields, 'submitted for approval' confirmation, 'requires backend' message when apiEnabled=false), added LiveReviews (filters useReviews data by product_id, shows live blockquotes when DB reviews exist, shows static demo blockquotes when offline, shows 'Be the first to leave a review' when API enabled but empty). commerce.tsx: imported LiveReviews and ReviewForm from shopping-ui, replaced the static hardcoded review blockquotes section in ProductDetailPage with LiveReviews + ReviewForm. Build passes with zero TypeScript/Vite errors across all three build environments (client, SSR, Nitro).
